findings.who: A filer currently claiming the American opportunity credit for a student with $2,000 or less of adjusted qualified education expenses, so Form 8863 line 4 (the 25% tier) is zero, and who also had an AOC denied or reduced for more than a math error or is within a 2- or 10-year bar.
findings.why_no: The tool computes f8863.aoc_claimed as false because it requires line 4 > $0; line 4 is zero when the credit consists only of the 100% first-$2,000 tier, so the ban question is never asked and f8863.ban_refused is set to false.
findings.irs_text: i8863 p. 3: 'This credit equals 100% of the first $2,000 and 25% of the next $2,000...'; i8863 p. 1: 'If your American opportunity credit was denied or reduced... you must attach a completed Form 8862... to your tax return for the next tax year for which you claim the credit.'
findings.fix: Gate on any AOC actually claimed (for example, Form 8863 line 6 or total AOC > $0, or Part I completed), not on line 4 being positive.

findings.who: A married-filing-jointly filer whose spouse, not the filer personally, had an AOC denied or reduced for more than a math error or was barred, while the joint return is claiming an AOC.
findings.why_no: The gated question asks whether 'you claimed' and the help says 'you filed Form 8862'; the filer reads this as only their own prior claim and answers No, although the joint return's AOC claim is affected by the spouse's prior denial or bar.
findings.irs_text: i8863 p. 1: 'If your American opportunity credit was denied or reduced... you must attach a completed Form 8862... to your tax return for the next tax year for which you claim the credit.'
findings.fix: Ask 'you or your spouse' in the question and help, and compute the refusal if either spouse has the prior denial, reduction, or bar.

findings.who: A filer whose AOC was denied or reduced for a pre-2016 tax year, with a final determination of fraud in 2016 or later, who is still within the 10-year fraud bar when claiming AOC for 2025.
findings.why_no: They read the Form 8862 rule's 'for any tax year beginning after 2015' as a cutoff and answer No to the 'ever denied/reduced or barred' question, missing that the p. 3 caution independently bars AOC for 10 years after the final determination.
findings.irs_text: i8863 p. 3: 'Don't claim the American opportunity credit for 2 years after there was a final determination that your claim was due to reckless or intentional disregard of the rules or 10 years after there was a final determination that your claim was due to fraud.'
findings.fix: State the 2- and 10-year bar separately with no 2015 cutoff, and ask whether any final determination of reckless disregard or fraud is still within its bar period.

findings.who: A filer whose prior AOC was denied or reduced for more than a math error and who later filed Form 8862, but the IRS did not allow the later claim (or had not yet allowed it), and who now answers No because they filed the form.
findings.why_no: The help says 'filed Form 8862... and it was allowed'; the filer reads only the filing requirement and answers No, although the line should remain true until a later Form 8862 claim is allowed.
findings.irs_text: i8863 p. 1: 'you must attach a completed Form 8862... to your tax return for the next tax year for which you claim the credit.'
findings.fix: Make the help say 'filed Form 8862 and the IRS allowed the credit on that later return,' and ask separately whether the later claim was allowed.

findings.who: A filer whose prior AOC was reduced (not denied) for more than a math error, and who did not later file an allowed Form 8862, but who answers No because the help only says 'after the denial or bar' and omits reductions.
findings.why_no: The question says 'denied or reduced,' but the help's clearing condition refers only to 'the denial or bar'; the filer reads a reduction as outside the help and answers No.
findings.irs_text: i8863 p. 1: 'If your American opportunity credit was denied or reduced for any reason other than a math or clerical error for any tax year beginning after 2015...'
findings.fix: Include 'reduction' in the help: 'after the denial, reduction, or bar.'

findings.who: A filer whose AOC for one student was denied or reduced for more than a math error, who is now claiming AOC for a different student, and who answers No because the prior denial was not for this student.
findings.why_no: They read the question as student-specific; the IRS rule applies to the next tax year for which the taxpayer claims the credit, not only the same student.
findings.irs_text: i8863 p. 1: 'If your American opportunity credit was denied or reduced... you must attach a completed Form 8862... to your tax return for the next tax year for which you claim the credit.'
findings.fix: Say 'for any student, including a different student' or ask broadly about any prior AOC denial, reduction, or bar by the taxpayer.

locators: p. 1, Form 8862 may be required, "If your American opportunity credit was denied or reduced for any reason other than a math or clerical error for any tax year beginning after 2015, you must attach a completed Form 8862, Information To Claim Certain Credits After Disallowance, to your tax return for the next tax year for which you claim the credit."
